process.heading: How to Remove a Nano Banana Watermark Online
process.intro: Start with the original exported image, keep a backup, and use the preview to judge the edited area. Workflow graphics below are illustrations of the steps.

steps.title: Choose your original image
steps.description: Upload one JPG, PNG or WebP image up to 10 MB. Use the original download rather than a screenshot when possible, so the tool has more detail to work with.

steps.title: Review the cost and process
steps.description: Sign in with Google to prepare your image. Check the displayed processing cost and available balance, then start the watermark removal. Selecting a file alone does not start processing.

steps.title: Inspect and download your JPG
steps.description: Compare the returned image with the original. Look closely at the former mark and nearby edges, shadows and textures. Download the edited JPG if the result works for your project.

items.question: How do I remove a visible Nano Banana watermark?
items.answer: Choose your saved JPG, PNG or WebP image, sign in with Google and review the cost in the workspace. Start processing, compare the returned image with the original, then download the edited JPG if the marked area looks suitable. Keep your original file.

items.question: Is Nano Banana watermark removal the same as Gemini watermark removal?
items.answer: Nano Banana is part of Google's Gemini image model family. This page uses WatermarkGemini's image watermark workflow to clean visible marks on saved images; it is not a separate Nano Banana model or an official Google service. Whether your image has a visible mark depends on where and how it was created.

items.question: Does this tool remove SynthID or make an image undetectable as AI?
items.answer: No. WatermarkGemini targets visible marks and does not claim to remove Google's invisible SynthID watermark or other provenance signals. A visually clean corner does not establish that an image is human-made or change how it was created.

items.question: Can I turn off visible watermarks in Gemini instead?
items.answer: Google documents a Media watermark option under Settings in Gemini Apps on a computer, subject to account and location restrictions. If available, it controls visible marks on newly generated media. It does not edit images you already saved or switch off SynthID and Content Credentials. Check Google's current help for availability.

items.question: Is the Nano Banana watermark remover free?
items.answer: Eligible standard image processing may use limited free image uses. Other processing may require credits. Sign in and review the applicable cost, balance and eligibility shown in the workspace before starting. The service does not offer unlimited free removal.

items.question: Which file formats and sizes are supported?
items.answer: Upload one JPG, PNG or WebP image up to 10 MB at a time. The watermark removal result is JPG. A PNG input does not mean the output will retain transparency. This page is for images, not PDF files, video or batch processing.

items.question: Can I remove the watermark without cropping?
items.answer: The tool processes the visible marked area rather than cutting away a corner. It aims to keep the full composition, but cleanup can change nearby details. Compare the result with the original, especially where the mark crosses fine textures, faces or text.

items.question: Do I need a Google account or my Gemini password?
items.answer: You can select and preview a file locally before signing in. Google sign-in to WatermarkGemini is required to prepare and process it. Upload the image you already downloaded; you do not need to give this service your Gemini password or connect your Gemini image history.

items.question: Will the edited image be identical to the original apart from the watermark?
items.answer: No pixel-identical result is guaranteed. Reconstructing a marked area may alter texture, edges or color, and the JPG result may have different compression from the source. Inspect the output at full size before including it in a final project.

items.question: Are the pictures on this page real removal results?
items.answer: No. The still life, landscape and texture images are original AI-generated illustrations of creative image uses. They were not generated with Nano Banana and do not demonstrate tested WatermarkGemini processing results. Judge cleanup quality using your own returned image.
